The Department of War is buying quantum sensors and clocks so the military can navigate and keep time without GPS, and it's laying the groundwork to buy quantum computers.

The Department of Commerce had NIST review the entire quantum industry. Kinsella believes it found the industry moving faster than anyone expected, which pushed the government to act. Commerce then picked a handful of companies to back, and Infleqtion signed a letter of intent for a $100 million investment.

The Department of Energy plans to put quantum computers in the national labs. Kinsella says it's the same playbook that put the first GPU clusters there, which helped lead to the AI boom we have today.

The key takeaway: Washington is tapping emergency fuel supplies to ease pressure from soaring energy costs.

posts.text:
This is unprecedented.

Micron, $MU, and Nvidia, $NVDA are expected to account for 36% of the S&P 500’s earnings growth in Q3 2026 earnings season.

This comes as $MU and $NVDA are expected to contribute +5.2 and +4.6 percentage points to the index’s +27% YoY earnings growth, respectively.

Meanwhile, the next 8 top contributors are projected to add +8.2 percentage points, accounting for ~30% of the estimated S&P 500’s net income growth.

Then, the remaining 490 stocks are set to contribute just +9.2 percentage points, representing 34% of the index’s projected earnings growth.

Excluding those top 10 contributors, earnings growth is estimated to decline -11% YoY in Q3.

Never in history have we witnessed market concentration like this.
